title: Lilac Clinic — virtual triage prototype field scratch
content:
Context: quick, messy capture from kickoff + technical sync with Lilac Clinic (3/2 call). They want a lightweight virtual triage assistant embedded in their patient portal: intake questions, risk triage (low/medium/high), recommended next step (self-care, schedule nurse call, urgent visit), and an audit trail for compliance. Primary ask is fast MVP by Q2 with an enterprise-ready path for PHI in production.

Attendees (3/2):
- Dr. Aisha Rahman (Lilac clinical lead)
- Tom Alvarez (Lilac Eng)
- Priya Patel (Redwood Solutions)
- Maya Chen (owner, CS)
- Omar Singh (platform eng)

High-level product notes:
- User flow: patient opens portal -> short symptom questionnaire (free-text + checkboxes) -> model suggests triage level + confidence + concise reasoning -> actionable next steps + scheduling link.
- Non-goal MVP: no full EHR writeback; only read and store triage record in patient folder.
- Must not generate diagnoses (avoid "definitive" medical claims). Preferred outputs: conservative, cite guideline bullets, link to internal care pathways.

Key constraints and requirements (prioritized):
1) PHI and data residency: initial pilot can use Redwood Dedicated in a cloud region that Lilac controls; long-term they want Private (VPC) on their GCP project or on-prem. KMS integration mandatory for any persistent logs.
2) Latency SLO: 95th <= 800ms for inference (text length avg ~120 tokens); interactive feel required. If Dedicated can't meet 95th at target, explore prefix caching for common openings.
3) Throughput: Clinic expects peak 120 req/min during morning window. Autoscale burst capacity good to have, but they require predictable cost envelope.
4) Audit trails: each decision needs a compact rationale blob stored (not raw model prompt), timestamp, model version, and model confidence score. Logs must be retained for 1 year and exportable to their SIEM.
5) Safety/regulatory guardrails: disallow medical prescriptions, always include fallback to "See a clinician" for ambiguous cases. Must detect suicide/self-harm language -> immediate escalation flow.
6) Integration: SSO via SAML, patient id mapping, read-only access to certain EHR fields (allergies, meds) via a proxy API. No writeback in MVP.

Technical gotchas called out in sync:
- EHR payloads are often messy; Tom said they will give a simplified clinical view endpoint, but it's rate-limited and can respond slowly (up to 600ms). Need to design request fan-out budget.
- PHI scrub rules: they want Redwood to not persist full original patient text in hosted logs. For Dedicated/Private we must confirm our log scrubbing + ability to disable request logging.
- Confidence calibration: Lilac expects a human-readable probability band (low/med/high) rather than raw logits. We'll need a mapping and documentation for clinicians.
- Prompt leakage risk: clinicians are worried about model revealing internal templates. We should use instruction templates that do not include PII and use KV cache separation across customers.

MVP acceptance criteria (proposal):
- End-to-end triage flow works in test environment with synthetic patient data (no PHI)
- 95p latency <= 800ms under normal load (50 r/min); degrade gracefully otherwise
- Audit trail produced for each session with model version, confidence band, and 1–2 rationale bullets
- Escalation flow triggers when keywords/score indicate serious risk (verified via test cases)
- Basic SAML SSO integration in staging

Suggested Redwood config for MVP:
- Deploy on Redwood Dedicated in us-central with reserved pool sized for baseline (50 r/min) + burst policy to 150. Set autoscale cooldown to 30s.
- Use a Llama2-analog 13B quantized variant we have in catalog with per-token latency tuned; enable KV prefix cache for common questionnaire openings.
- Turn on structured-output constraints (JSON schema) to force fields: {triage_level, confidence_band, rationale[], next_step_action}.
- Enable canary rollout (10% of traffic) for model updates and manual review window.

Sample prompt/template sketches (for engineering):
- System: "You are a clinical triage assistant. Provide a conservative triage recommendation. Never provide definitive diagnoses or prescriptions. If text indicates possible self-harm, escalate immediately."
- User (concatenated): "Symptoms: {patient_free_text}\nAge: {age}\nAllergies: {allergies}\nMeds: {meds}\nClinical context: {context}\n\nReturn ONLY JSON with keys: triage_level, confidence_band, rationale (list), next_step_action, escalation_flag (boolean)."

Edge cases to test (must add to evaluation set):
- Short ambiguous phrases: "I feel off"
- Long multi-symptom paragraphs with medication lists (ensure token limits handled)
- Non-English inputs — initial plan: reject with polite ask to re-enter in English or route to human
- Data-corrupt EHR fields -> fallback to questionnaire-only flow

Operational runbook notes (initial):
- If Dedicated pool latency > 900ms on 95p: fallback to cheaper/smaller model variant routed via smart routing and mark in audit trail; notify ops channel.
- If SAML auth failures > 3% per hour: circuit-break authentication and serve a maintenance banner.
- Escalation: when escalation_flag true, create task in Lilac ticketing (they will connect via webhook) and mark patient record; notify on-call clinician per their SLA.

Questions (open items for Lilac):
- Data retention: they said 1 year but need to confirm whether condensed rationale-only records are OK vs full transcript.
- Which SIEM endpoint and auth method for log export? (SFTP vs HTTPS with mTLS?)
- Can they provide a small set (~500) of de-identified triage transcripts for calibration?

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Priya: draft minimal security checklist for Dedicated vs Private (due 3/6).
- Omar: run quick perf estimate for 13B quantized variant with KV caching at expected request mix (due 3/5).
- Maya: send follow-up email with sample prompt templates + ask for retention confirmation + request de-id dataset (today).
- Tom (Lilac): share SAML metadata + simplified clinical view API contract (by 3/8).

Testing plan sketch (for eng + QA):
- Create synthetic evaluation corpus (500 examples) covering edge cases listed above.
- Unit tests for JSON schema validation and schema drift detection.
- Safety tests: trigger keywords, hallucination probes, and regression alerts on reasoning bullets.

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Consider Redwood Optimize suggestion engine to see whether smaller model (7B q4) could meet latency SLO with similar quality; cost delta will matter to Lilac.
- Could offer staged deployment: start Dedicated-hosted hybrid -> Private once data policy signed. That reduces time-to-MVP.
- Need clear customer-facing language: "triage assistant — not a diagnostic tool" on UI and in ToS.

Action items (short):
- Email w/ prompt templates + retention ask (Maya) — today
- Perf microbenchmark (Omar) — 3/5
- Security checklist draft (Priya) — 3/6
- Receive SAML + API contract (Tom) — 3/8

Slack breadcrumbs / links to save: #clinic-integration thread (see pinned messages), recording: drive:/meet-recordings/lilac-2026-03-02.mp4 (TBD), Confluence spec page (linked above).

End messy scratch — will refine into a tidy onboarding checklist once we have SAML + perf numbers.
